passages.original: 9. Tertium imitati sunt Africani episcopi, per epistolam quæ collationis Carthag.|cognit. a, ap. 16, inserta esi, quaeque apud Augustinum exstat epist. 128, Donatistis pollicentes, eos a se, si convicti ad unitatem redierint, sic recipiendos esse, « ut non solum viam salutis inveniant, sed nec honorem episcopatus amittant. Poterit quippe, inquiunt, unusquisque nostrum , honoris sibi socio copulato , vicissim sedere eminentius, sicut peregrino episcopo juxta considente collega. Hoc cum alternis basilicis utrisque conceditur, uterque ab alterutro, mutuo honore praevenitur : quia ubi præceptio charitatis dilataverit corda, possessio pacis non fit angusta;
passages.english: 9. The third [course] was followed by the African bishops, in the letter which is inserted in the Conference of Carthage, first day of proceedings, chapter 16, and which survives among Augustine's letters as letter 128, promising the Donatists that, if once convicted they returned to unity, they would be received by them in such a way "that they not only find the way of salvation, but also do not lose the honour of the episcopate. For each one of us," they say, "with a partner in honour joined to him, will be able to sit in the more prominent place in turn, just as [happens] when a visiting bishop sits beside his colleague. When this is granted to both in alternate basilicas, each is anticipated by the other in mutual honour: for where the precept of charity has enlarged hearts, the possession of peace is not made narrow;
passages.notes: "Tertium" refers to a third option or precedent described before this passage; the reference is not clear without the preceding text. "collationis Carthag. cognit. a, ap. 16" is garbled by scanning. It is taken as "cognit. 1, cap. 16" (first session, chapter 16). "esi" read as "est". "praevenitur" (is anticipated, i.e. outdone or preceded in showing honour) is rendered literally.
